rituals.name: FOLD THE NEXT STEP
rituals.goal: Give the unfinished thing somewhere physical to live besides your head.
rituals.mission: Give the unfinished thing somewhere physical to live besides your head.
rituals.rule: Guess whether your mind will keep rehearsing the task after the next action is captured externally.
rituals.one_rule: Guess whether your mind will keep rehearsing the task after the next action is captured externally.
rituals.play: Write exactly one next physical action on a small piece of paper: “email Sam,” “open invoice,” “put form in bag.” Fold the paper and place it where you will see it later.
rituals.twist: Wait ten seconds and check whether the task feels equally necessary to rehearse.
rituals.mindBend: A task can repeat in your mind when it has nowhere else to live.
rituals.mind_bend: A task can repeat in your mind when it has nowhere else to live.
rituals.why: A captured next step can reduce the brain’s need to keep an unfinished intention active.
rituals.reveal: A captured next step can reduce the brain’s need to keep an unfinished intention active.
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Keep the written version small, reversible and safe. Do not use momentum as a reason to ignore pain, exhaustion, major consequences or information that needs more thought. Keep the result tied to this one example rather than generalising it to every situation.

rituals.name: 2× CARTOON REPLAY
rituals.goal: Your loop has been using prestige-drama pacing.
rituals.mission: Your loop has been using prestige-drama pacing.
rituals.rule: Guess whether the thought feels equally authoritative at ridiculous double speed.
rituals.one_rule: Guess whether the thought feels equally authoritative at ridiculous double speed.
rituals.play: Replay the exact thought in your head at absurdly fast cartoon speed. No pausing for emotional emphasis. Run it through three times.
rituals.twist: Check if it becomes harder to treat each phrase like a solemn revelation.
rituals.mindBend: A thought can feel profound partly because you keep giving it dramatic pacing.
rituals.mind_bend: A thought can feel profound partly because you keep giving it dramatic pacing.
rituals.why: Processing style changes emotional weight even when the words are identical.
rituals.reveal: Processing style changes emotional weight even when the words are identical.
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not repeat the memory/imagery pass until it feels 'finished'. If you are replaying rather than learning something new, stop and switch attention. The result is a working perspective, not proof that the opposite story is true.

rituals.name: WRONG VOICE CASTING
rituals.goal: Your thought has been badly typecast as “serious narrator.”
rituals.mission: Your thought has been badly typecast as “serious narrator.”
rituals.rule: Guess which absurd voice makes the loop lose the most authority.
rituals.one_rule: Guess which absurd voice makes the loop lose the most authority.

rituals.twist: Check if the message feels different when the speaker identity changes.
rituals.mindBend: A thought does not become wiser because it uses your most convincing inner voice.
rituals.mind_bend: A thought does not become wiser because it uses your most convincing inner voice.

rituals.name: LOOP COUNTER
rituals.goal: Stop arguing with the thought.
rituals.mission: Stop arguing with the thought.
rituals.rule: Guess how many times the same theme will return in thirty seconds.
rituals.one_rule: Guess how many times the same theme will return in thirty seconds.
rituals.play: For 30 sec, do nothing to stop the loop. Each time it returns, tap one finger. No analysis, just count entrances.
rituals.twist: Compare the count with your prediction and notice whether counting changes the rhythm.
rituals.mindBend: The moment you can count a thought, you are not completely inside it.
rituals.mind_bend: The moment you can count a thought, you are not completely inside it.
rituals.why: Measuring a loop turns you from participant into observer for a moment.
rituals.reveal: Measuring a loop turns you from participant into observer for a moment.
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use this pass as an interruption, not a new way to rehearse the loop. One deliberate pass is enough. If the same pattern returns later, re-check the new context rather than copying today's answer.

rituals.name: CLOSE ONE TAB
rituals.goal: Do not organise your whole life.
rituals.mission: Do not organise your whole life.
rituals.rule: Guess whether finishing one two-minute loose end changes the mental noise at all.
rituals.one_rule: Guess whether finishing one two-minute loose end changes the mental noise at all.
rituals.play: Name three open loops. Pick the smallest one that can be genuinely finished in under two minutes—send, file, throw away, book, put away, confirm. Finish only that one.
rituals.twist: Check if the other two feel even slightly less crowded after one closure.
rituals.mindBend: You do not have to clear the whole desk to prove that tabs can close.
rituals.mind_bend: You do not have to clear the whole desk to prove that tabs can close.
rituals.why: Completion gives the brain a concrete signal that not every open loop is permanent.
rituals.reveal: Completion gives the brain a concrete signal that not every open loop is permanent.
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Keep the naming step from becoming another rumination ritual. End it when the planned step is complete, even if the thought still feels unfinished. Stop at the planned endpoint rather than repeating the ritual until it feels completely convincing.

rituals.name: REVERSE THE MEMORY
rituals.goal: Your memory keeps taking the same road.
rituals.mission: Your memory keeps taking the same road.
rituals.rule: Guess which detail becomes harder to connect when the story runs from end to beginning.
rituals.one_rule: Guess which detail becomes harder to connect when the story runs from end to beginning.
rituals.play: Start at the final moment of the memory. Step backward scene by scene until the beginning. Don’t explain causes—only move backward through observable moments.
rituals.twist: Catch where the usual “and therefore…” story becomes awkward to maintain.
rituals.mindBend: A memory feels inevitable partly because you always replay it in the same direction.
rituals.mind_bend: A memory feels inevitable partly because you always replay it in the same direction.
rituals.why: Narrative order creates causal smoothness. Reverse order disrupts that automatic storyline.
rituals.reveal: Narrative order creates causal smoothness. Reverse order disrupts that automatic storyline.
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Keep the memory pass brief and do not dig for detail that is not coming naturally. Stop if the scene becomes overwhelming, you feel detached/unreal, or you start replaying it compulsively.

rituals.name: NUMBER GATE
rituals.goal: Put three numbers in the doorway and make the loop squeeze past them.
rituals.mission: Put three numbers in the doorway and make the loop squeeze past them.
rituals.rule: Guess whether the sentence stays perfectly intact while you insert 7–2–9 between its phrases.
rituals.one_rule: Guess whether the sentence stays perfectly intact while you insert 7–2–9 between its phrases.
rituals.play: Repeat the loop, but after every short phrase say “seven, two, nine” in your head. Do two passes.
rituals.twist: Notice any loss of rhythm, urgency or verbatim precision.
rituals.mindBend: A thought can feel unstoppable until something occupies the machinery that keeps replaying it.

rituals.unique_game_move: DID YOU INVENT IT OR REMEMBER IT?
rituals.mechanism_fingerprint: For a newly generated idea, search for plausible prior exposures whose content may be remembered without source information.
rituals.ritualText:
PLAY TIME
70 sec

GAME
DID YOU INVENT IT OR REMEMBER IT?

GOAL
A familiar idea can return without its source tag and feel brand new.

ONE RULE
Guess whether you've encountered this idea before in a conversation, article, video, or old note.

PLAY
Take a sudden 'original' idea. Search your own recent memory for possible source exposures before claiming novelty.

TWIST
Notice how idea familiarity can survive after source memory fades.

MIND BEND
Original-feeling is not proof of original origin.

SAFETY
PAUSE
Keep the example you picked tentative: memory can shift with attention and framing. Do not turn a recalled detail into certainty without independent evidence. The result is a working perspective, not proof that the opposite story is true.

rituals.name: FAMILIARITY WITHOUT A FILE
rituals.goal: Sometimes the feeling of familiarity arrives without a matching memory file.
rituals.mission: Sometimes the feeling of familiarity arrives without a matching memory file.
rituals.rule: Guess whether 'this feels familiar' always means you can retrieve a specific earlier event.
rituals.one_rule: Guess whether 'this feels familiar' always means you can retrieve a specific earlier event.
rituals.play: When a harmless déjà-vu-like familiarity occurs, separate FAMILIAR FEELING from RETRIEVABLE MEMORY. Ask what exact prior event you can name.
rituals.twist: Check if the signal exists without a source.
rituals.mindBend: A familiarity signal can be real even when the story attached to it is uncertain.
rituals.mind_bend: A familiarity signal can be real even when the story attached to it is uncertain.
rituals.why: Familiarity and recollection are separable memory processes.
rituals.reveal: Familiarity and recollection are separable memory processes.
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Treat this pass as a memory exercise, not a reconstruction of objective proof. Do not fill missing detail just to make the story coherent. Keep the result tied to this one example rather than generalising it to every situation.

rituals.one_rule: Guess what you can remember before looking again.

rituals.twist: Notice how the missing pieces become more memorable after effortful retrieval.
rituals.mindBend: Struggle can be the part that teaches.
rituals.mind_bend: Struggle can be the part that teaches.

rituals.mission: If practice feels perfect, your brain may be doing too little.
rituals.rule: Guess which change makes retrieval harder but still possible.
rituals.one_rule: Guess which change makes retrieval harder but still possible.

rituals.twist: Check if performance feels worse while thinking becomes deeper.
rituals.mindBend: Easy today and remembered tomorrow are not the same target.
rituals.mind_bend: Easy today and remembered tomorrow are not the same target.
rituals.why: Some difficulties improve long-term learning despite reducing short-term fluency.
rituals.reveal: Some difficulties improve long-term learning despite reducing short-term fluency.
rituals.safety:

rituals.name: DON'T PLAY MEMORY WHACK-A-MOLE
rituals.goal: Fighting a memory can turn the session into nothing but memory-monitoring.
rituals.mission: Fighting a memory can turn the session into nothing but memory-monitoring.
rituals.rule: Guess how often you must check for the memory to know you're successfully 'not thinking' it.
rituals.one_rule: Guess how often you must check for the memory to know you're successfully 'not thinking' it.
rituals.play: For one harmless intrusive memory, replace 'Don’t remember' with 'I notice the memory is available; I'm returning to X.' No checking whether it left.
rituals.twist: Notice the drop in monitoring work.
rituals.mindBend: You cannot verify a memory is absent without searching for it.
rituals.mind_bend: You cannot verify a memory is absent without searching for it.
rituals.why: Intentional suppression requires monitoring for the target and can become effortful or paradoxical.
rituals.reveal: Intentional suppression requires monitoring for the target and can become effortful or paradoxical.
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use this pass to calibrate confidence, not to reach 100% certainty. Stop if you notice yourself repeating it just to feel sure. A single pass can test the pattern; it does not need to settle it permanently.

rituals.name: DOORWAY STOLE THE THOUGHT
rituals.goal: You walked into the room and the reason for walking there evaporated.
rituals.mission: You walked into the room and the reason for walking there evaporated.
rituals.rule: Guess whether returning to the previous location helps the intention come back.
rituals.one_rule: Guess whether returning to the previous location helps the intention come back.
rituals.play: Next time a harmless intention vanishes after a doorway, mentally reconstruct the previous room, posture, and last action—or physically return if practical.
rituals.twist: Check if the old context restores the thought.
rituals.mindBend: The thought may be behind a context boundary, not gone.
rituals.mind_bend: The thought may be behind a context boundary, not gone.
rituals.why: Event boundaries update working memory and can reduce access to prior goals.
rituals.reveal: Event boundaries update working memory and can reduce access to prior goals.
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use this pass to reduce mind-reading, not to manufacture reassurance. Direct communication and boundaries carry more weight than guessed motives. If the same pattern returns later, re-check the new context rather than copying today's answer.
